chapter_guidelines.content:
The ICD-10-CM provides codes for different types of myocardial 
infarction. Type 1 myocardial infarctions are assigned to codes I21.0-
I21.4. 
 
Type 2 myocardial infarction (myocardial infarction due to demand 
ischemia or secondary to ischemic imbalance) is assigned to code 
I21.A1, Myocardial infarction type 2 with the underlying cause coded 
first, if applicable. Do not assign code I24.89, Other forms of acute 
ischemic heart disease, for the demand ischemia. If a type 2 AMI is 
described as NSTEMI or STEMI, only assign code I21.A1. Codes 
I21.01-I21.4 should only be assigned for type 1 AMIs.  
 
Acute myocardial infarctions type 3, 4a, 4b, 4c and 5 are assigned to 
code I21.A9, Other myocardial infarction type. 
 
 
 
 
 
The "Code also" and "Code first" notes should be followed related to 
 
 
 
 complications, and for coding of postprocedural myocardial infarctions 
 
 
 
 during or following cardiac surgery.
chapter_guidelines.title: Other Types of Myocardial Infarction

chapter_guidelines.content:
infarction (STEMI) and non-
ST elevation myocardial infarction (NSTEMI) 
The ICD-10-CM codes for type 1 acute myocardial infarction (AMI) 
identify the site, such as anterolateral wall or true posterior wall. 
Subcategories I21.0-I21.2 and code I21.3 are used for type 1 ST 
elevation myocardial infarction (STEMI). Code I21.4, Non-ST elevation 
(NSTEMI) myocardial infarction, is used for type 1 non-ST elevation 
myocardial infarction (NSTEMI) and nontransmural MIs. 
 
If a type 1 NSTEMI evolves to STEMI, assign the STEMI code. If a type 
1 STEMI converts to NSTEMI due to thrombolytic therapy, it is still 
coded as STEMI. 
 
For encounters occurring while the myocardial infarction is equal to, or 
less than, four weeks old, including transfers to another acute setting or a 
postacute setting, and the myocardial infarction meets the definition for 
“other diagnoses” (see Section III, Reporting Additional Diagnoses), 
codes from category I21 may continue to be reported. For encounters 
after the 4-week time frame and the patient is still receiving care related 
to the myocardial infarction, the appropriate aftercare code should be 
assigned, rather than a code from category I21. For old or healed 
myocardial infarctions not requiring further care, code I25.2, Old 
myocardial infarction, may be assigned.

Encounter Summary:
- Chart excerpt documents an acute myocardial infarction with cardiology documentation of “NSTEMI.”
- Troponin is reported to have peaked at 4.2.
- No diagnosis code is documented in the chart excerpt.

Documentation Gaps:
1. Gap: MI type is not fully specified for ICD-10-CM assignment.
- Why it matters: ICD-10-CM distinguishes type 1 NSTEMI from type 2 MI and other MI types. Per guideline, code I21.4 applies to type 1 NSTEMI, while type 2 MI is coded to I21.A1 and other MI types to I21.A9.
- Evidence quote: “Cardiology note says ‘NSTEMI’.”
- Evidence quote: “Patient with acute myocardial infarction.”
- Minimal clarification needed: Please clarify whether the documented NSTEMI represents type 1 MI, type 2 MI, or another MI type if known.

2. Gap: Timing/episode relative to the acute MI window is not documented in the excerpt.
- Why it matters: ICD-10-CM category I21 is used for encounters when the MI is equal to or less than 4 weeks old; after that, different coding may apply.
- Evidence quote: “Patient with acute myocardial infarction.”
- Minimal clarification needed: Confirm whether this encounter is for an acute MI within 4 weeks of onset/current treatment episode.

3. Gap: If the MI is not type 1, the underlying cause or related circumstance is not documented.
- Why it matters: For type 2 MI, ICD-10-CM guideline states the underlying cause is coded first, if applicable.
- Evidence quote: “Cardiology note says ‘NSTEMI’.”
- Minimal clarification needed: If this is not type 1 MI, clarify the underlying precipitating condition/circumstance, if clinically determined and documented elsewhere.

Proposed Provider Queries:
1. Topic: Clarification of myocardial infarction type.
- Reason query is needed: “NSTEMI” alone does not establish whether this is type 1 NSTEMI versus type 2 or another MI type for compliant code assignment.
- Evidence quote: “Cardiology note says ‘NSTEMI’.”
- Evidence quote: “Troponin peaked at 4.2.”
- Non-leading query text: “The record documents ‘acute myocardial infarction’ and a cardiology note stating ‘NSTEMI,’ with troponin peaking at 4.2. For documentation specificity, please clarify the type of myocardial infarction for this encounter, if known.”
- Suggested response options:
  - Type 1 NSTEMI
  - Type 2 myocardial infarction
  - Other myocardial infarction type
  - Myocardial injury without myocardial infarction
  - Clinically undetermined
  - Other: ______

2. Topic: Clarification of acuity/timing of the MI.
- Reason query is needed: Coding for AMI depends on whether the encounter is within the acute 4-week period.
- Evidence quote: “Patient with acute myocardial infarction.”
- Non-leading query text: “The chart documents acute myocardial infarction. For documentation specificity, please clarify whether this encounter is for an acute myocardial infarction within 4 weeks of onset/current treatment episode, if known.”
- Suggested response options:
  - Acute MI within 4 weeks/current episode of care
  - Follow-up care after acute MI beyond 4 weeks
  - History of prior MI only
  - Clinically undetermined
  - Other: ______

Coding Specificity Checklist:
- MI type: type 1, type 2, or other MI type
- If NSTEMI is type 1, document explicitly as type 1 NSTEMI
- If not type 1, document the underlying cause/circumstance when clinically determined
- Acuity/timing: whether the MI is within the acute 4-week window
- Any evolution/conversion if applicable (for example, if NSTEMI evolved to STEMI) — not documented in this excerpt

Risk Flags:
- “NSTEMI” is documented, but MI type is not explicitly stated; coding cannot be assumed from the excerpt alone.
- No evidence in the excerpt of STEMI, infarct site, culprit vessel, or postprocedural MI; these should not be queried based on current evidence.
- Insufficient evidence to query complications, demand ischemia, coronary artery involvement, or procedural relationship beyond the MI-type clarification above.
